LOCATION: Tiny Kolkata tea counter with chipped cups and a crowded back wall. LIGHT AND ATMOSPHERE: Warm tungsten from stall mixed with cool drizzle outside. CONTINUITY LOCK: Cup positions, wet patches and Naisha's outfit remain continuous. WORLD RULES: Naturalistic feature-film storytelling; calibrated emotional restraint, uninterrupted character identity, and observable human behavior. Avoid frantic montage, plastic beauty lighting, abrupt perspective flips, lip-sync drift, or unmotivated camera swoops.

SHOT 1 (00–02s) — 28 mm wide framing through a doorway or street edge, no distorted faces. See Naisha speaking quickly at a corner counter while Zain holds his clay cup and listens. Light stays motivated by the real street, sky or practical source; hold skin texture and natural color without glamour relighting. Establish the physical axis, dominant light direction and relative distances; subsequent cuts must preserve them.

SHOT 2 (02–05s) — 50 mm eye-height shoulder-follow, stabilized and quiet. Track gently past a boiling kettle into a clearer two-shot; her sentences overlap slightly as she avoids the real topic. Reflections and background motion remain subtle so a quiet glance is readable; there is no sudden color or wardrobe jump. Match the character's motion across the cut, not merely the background shape; preserve prop orientation and the screen-side of each participant.

SHOT 3 (05–07s) — 65 mm side-profile two-shot with depth from stationary background figures. She stops to blow on tea and realizes he's smiling at her nervousness rather than mocking it. Leave audible room for the environment and a natural breath; do not cover the reaction with a fast insert. Hold the reaction before redirecting attention, keeping shoulders, eye-lines and contact with the environment continuous.

SHOT 4 (07–10s) — 55 mm settled medium that holds half a beat beyond the spoken or silent response. He responds with a single gentle line; her shoulders release as a customer passes naturally through background. End on behavior rather than a posed smile; carry the emotional change into the next cut without an artificial flourish. Finish on the stated physical end position, with no reset of the blocking; use a straight cut or a natural hold, never a dissolve that changes the geography.

AUDIO / SOUND: Tea boiling, glass clinks and rain at shop shutter; Only location sound and believable dialogue or breathing; any music must be explicitly requested rather than added by default. EDIT / DELIVERY: Four distinct framings, motivated cuts, character and prop locks across shots; no duplicate angles posing as coverage. Maintain screen direction, plausible exposure and environment continuity from opening frame to final hold.
